card.name: Gule Wamkulu
card.tagline: Chewa Nyau masked spirit dance of the dead
card.profile: Gule Wamkulu ('the great dance') is the masked ritual dance of the Chewa Nyau brotherhood, a secret society of initiated men in Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique (UNESCO ICH; Britannica). Performed at funerals, initiations (chinamwali), the installation or death of chiefs, and after the July harvest, dancers in wood-and-straw masks and costumes embody zilombo - spirits of the dead and wild animals (antelope, lions) as well as figures like slave traders and even helicopters - each character teaching moral and social lessons (UNESCO ICH; Nyau, Wikipedia). It dates to the 17th-century Chewa Empire.
card.insight: Within the Chewa's matrilineal society the Nyau gave married men solidarity and authority; the masked dancers are regarded as actual spirits, not men, and must not be named as such. UNESCO proclaimed Gule Wamkulu a Masterpiece in 2005 and inscribed it in 2008 (UNESCO ICH).
